security_audit.summary: Adjudicated all 309 static findings for the official Anthropics hook-development skill; every finding is a false positive. The high/critical hits (dd/mkfs/rm -rf, /etc and /sys writes, path traversal) are literal detection strings inside defensive PreToolUse validation hooks that DENY those operations, or example inputs illustrating blocked commands. The remaining medium/low hits are ordinary shell idioms (jq parsing, $(cat), /tmp state, documentation code fences). No prompt injection, data-exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: The database-logging example in references/advanced.md interpolates hook input directly into a SQL string ($input) via psql, illustrating an SQL-injection-prone pattern.
remediation.suggestion: Update the example to use parameterized queries so readers do not copy an injectable pattern into their own hooks.

content.user_title: Build Claude Code Plugin Hooks with Confidence
content.value_statement: Writing Claude Code hooks means juggling event names, JSON schemas, and shell boilerplate that are easy to get wrong. This skill gives Claude the reference material, examples, and validators needed to produce correct command-based and prompt-based hooks on the first try.
actual_capabilities: Generates command-type and prompt-type hooks for all Claude Code events, including PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, and Notification.
Produces the correct hooks.json wrapper format for plugins and the direct format for user settings.
Provides working example hooks for validating Bash commands, guarding file writes, and loading project context at session start.
Explains the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, and CLAUDE_ENV_FILE variables and how hooks read stdin and signal decisions via exit codes and JSON.
Includes shell scripts to lint hook scripts and validate hooks.json against the expected schema.
Covers advanced patterns such as caching, rate limiting, audit logging, and migrating command hooks to prompt-based hooks.
limitations: It teaches hook authoring and shape; it does not execute or deploy hooks into a live Claude Code installation for you.
The example validation hooks are illustrative starting points, not a complete security policy; real deployments need review and hardening.
Guidance targets Claude Code plugin and settings hooks specifically and does not cover unrelated automation frameworks.

use_cases.title: Block dangerous shell commands
use_cases.description: Create a PreToolUse hook that inspects Bash tool input and denies destructive or privileged commands before they run.
use_cases.target_user: Platform engineers hardening a shared Claude Code setup

use_cases.title: Load project context automatically
use_cases.description: Write a SessionStart hook that detects the project type and exports environment variables so every session starts with the right context.

use_cases.title: Migrate to prompt-based validation
use_cases.description: Convert brittle string-matching command hooks into prompt-based hooks that reason about intent, using the migration reference.

prompt_templates.title: Simple command hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PreToolUse hook that logs every Bash command to a file before it runs.

prompt_templates.title: Validation hook with decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a PreToolUse hook that denies rm -rf commands and asks for confirmation on sudo commands, returning the correct JSON decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: exit codes and permission decisions

prompt_templates.title: Prompt-based hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a prompt-based PostToolUse hook that reviews file writes for accidental secrets and explains any concern it finds.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prompt-type hooks over command scripts

prompt_templates.title: Full plugin hook set
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a hooks.json for my plugin with a SessionStart context loader, a PreToolUse Bash validator, and a Stop hook that runs tests, then validate the schema.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: multi-event plugin with schema validation

output_examples.input: Create a PreToolUse hook that blocks rm -rf commands.
output_examples.output: A ready-to-use Bash hook script that reads the tool input from stdin, extracts the command with jq, and returns a deny decision when it detects rm -rf, plus the hooks.json entry that wires it to the PreToolUse event.

output_examples.input: Add a SessionStart hook that detects whether my project uses TypeScript.
output_examples.output: A SessionStart hook that changes into the project directory, checks for package.json and tsconfig.json, and appends the detected project type to the session environment file so later steps can react to it.

best_practices: Always read hook input from stdin and parse it with jq rather than assuming a fixed shape.
Signal decisions explicitly with the documented exit codes and JSON output so Claude Code can allow, ask, or deny reliably.
Validate hooks.json against the schema and test each hook with sample input before deploying it to real sessions.
anti_patterns: Interpolating raw hook input directly into shell or SQL commands, which invites injection.
Relying only on brittle substring matching for security decisions instead of clear allow and deny rules or prompt-based review.
Writing hooks that fail silently, leaving users unsure whether a decision was made.

faq.question: What hook events does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers all Claude Code hook events, including PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, and Notification.

faq.question: What is the difference between command hooks and prompt-based hooks?
faq.answer: Command hooks run a shell script and return decisions through exit codes and JSON. Prompt-based hooks ask Claude to reason about the situation, which suits nuanced checks that are hard to express as string matching.

faq.question: Do I put hooks in hooks.json or in settings?
faq.answer: Plugins use a hooks.json file with a wrapper format, while user settings use a direct format in the settings file. The skill generates the correct shape for each case.

faq.question: How do I reference files inside my plugin from a hook?
faq.answer: Use the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT variable, which points at your plugin root, so hooks keep working regardless of where the plugin is installed.

faq.question: Can hooks block a tool from running?
faq.answer: Yes. A PreToolUse hook can return a deny decision to stop a tool call, an ask decision to require confirmation, or allow the call to proceed.

faq.question: How do I test a hook before using it?
faq.answer: The skill includes a test script and a schema validator. You pass sample JSON input to your hook and confirm it returns the expected decision, then validate the hooks file against the schema.
